title: Aiden and Betty and the Bully
reason: Rewrite an over-complex and potentially victim-blaming bullying arc as clear, age-appropriate safeguarding guidance: speak clearly, walk away, and tell a trusted adult.

pages.1: A boy in Year 2 was called Marcus. He kept calling Aiden a silly name. Aiden did not like it.
pages.2: Aiden went home feeling quiet and upset. He told Betty what had happened.
pages.3: "That is not okay," Betty said. "You can tell him to stop. Then we can tell a grown-up."
pages.4: That night, Aiden made a plan. He would speak clearly, walk away, and tell Miss Okafor. Socks sat beside him.
pages.5: On Friday, Marcus used the silly name again. Betty looked at him. "His name is Aiden. Please stop," she said.
pages.6: Aiden was glad Betty helped. He wanted to try the words himself next time. "I will stand with you," Betty said.
pages.7: On Monday, Marcus said it again. Aiden faced him. "My name is Aiden. Stop," he said in a clear voice.
pages.8: Aiden walked away with Betty. They told Miss Okafor what had happened. She listened and said she would help.
pages.9: That evening, Aiden felt proud. He had spoken clearly, walked away, and asked for help. Socks rested by his feet.
pages.10: Betty put a hand on Aiden's shoulder. "You did well," she said.
pages.11: A week later, Marcus bumped Aiden's tray by accident. "Sorry, Aiden," Marcus said. Aiden nodded.
pages.12: Miss Okafor talked with the class about bullying. "If someone keeps being unkind, tell them to stop and tell an adult," she said.
pages.13: "You can speak, move away, and ask for help," Miss Okafor said. "Bullying is never your fault." Aiden remembered her words.
